title: Percentile latency + link-grade region steering
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Region-level routing currently uses simple latency thresholds and single-signal link health checks which cause oscillation for mixed workloads (short chat vs long generation) and unexpected failovers during transient network noise. This ticket implements a percentile-aware steering policy that fuses p50/p95 latency profiles with a compact link-grade score (packet loss, jitter, and streak errors) to make region selection more stable and service-aware. The goal is to prefer regions that minimize tail-latency regressions for heavy requests while avoiding unsafe cross-region failovers during short-lived blips.
acceptance_criteria: Policy implementation available behind feature flag (region_steering_v2)
Region selection API returns chosen_region and rationale fields for every decision
Observed client-facing p95 SLO regressions reduced by >=20% in synthetic mixed workload test compared to baseline
No increase in request-level re-routes >0.5% during steady-state traffic
Graceful fallback to compatible model variant mapping documented and triggered when region capacity or link-grade is degraded
Unit + e2e tests covering telemetry staleness, percentile fusion, and variant fallback behaviors
design_notes: Core signal set: rolling p50 and p95 computed per-region over 5m and 1h windows plus link-grade = weighted combination of recent packet-loss, jitter, and consecutive error streaks (scaled 0-100).
Percentile fusion: compute a composite latency score = alpha * p95 + (1-alpha) * p50 where alpha is workload-weighted (default alpha=0.7 for generation-heavy customers, alpha=0.4 for chat-heavy).
Stability term: apply temporal smoothing with exponential decay to reduce flip-flopping; hold decisions for a minimum of 30s unless link-grade breaches an emergency threshold.
Capacity-aware adjustment: penalize regions by utilization factor to avoid choosing a low-latency but saturated POP; map utilization into a 0-1 penalty applied to composite score.

Fallback mapping: have an explicit mapping table of compatible model variants (e.g., quantized/llm-v2-small) per region tier. When chosen region is unhealthy, route to nearest region with compatible variant and degrade model to maintain latency SLOs.
Observability: decision rationale string should include p50,p95,link-grade,utilization,stability-score and selected-fallback (if any).
decisions: Use p50 + p95 fusion (no single-percentile policy) to account for mixed request shapes
Link-grade score will be normalized per-region using historical baselines to accommodate differences in ISP characteristics
Minimum decision hold (hysteresis) set to 30s; emergency override if link-grade > 85
Variant fallback will prefer same-model-family quantized variants before switching families to preserve output characteristics
tasks: Implement aggregator to emit per-region p50/p95 windows and normalized link-grade (ENG infra change)
Add new region selector module with composite scoring and hysteresis logic
Extend routing API to return decision rationale fields and chosen_fallback_variant
Create compatibility matrix for model variants and region tiers with engineering-approved fallbacks
Add integration tests with synthetic mixed workload generator (short/long requests)
Dashboard: per-region composite score, selected region counts, fallback events over time
Gradual rollout: feature flag + 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring alerts
metrics: Rate of cross-region re-routes per 10k requests
Fallback events per 10k requests and top fallback targets
Decision stability (fraction of decisions that change within 60s)
Model variant switch frequency and associated quality regression signals
rollout_plan: Deploy selector behind region_steering_v2 feature flag in staging and run canary traffic for 24h
Enable for 5% of production traffic with close monitoring of p95 and re-route rate
If metrics stable, increment to 25% for 48h and run prompt-set quality checks for any variant fallbacks
Full enablement after no regressions for 7 days; keep emergency kill switch for 1 week post-rollout
Coordinate with SE and Solutions teams for high-usage customers to opt into custom alpha weight settings
testing_plan: Unit tests for percentile fusion math and weight decay
Integration tests: simulated POP degradation (packet loss spike) and ensure emergency override triggers fallback
E2E: mixed-generator workload (70% short chat, 30% long generation) comparing baseline and new selector
Chaos test: random transient network noise at 1% of regions to validate hysteresis behavior
Quality gate: automated evals on canonical prompt set when variant fallback occurs
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect normalization of link-grade causes consistent bias toward/against certain POPs. Mitigation: add baseline calibration job and manual sanity checks before rollout.
Risk: Variant fallbacks produce subtle quality regressions. Mitigation: conservative fallback ordering (same-family first) and additional eval hooks with alerting when quality delta > threshold.
Risk: Increased complexity in decision rationale increases payload size. Mitigation: return compact rationale code and reserve full explanation to logs/backtrace on demand.
Risk: Oscillation under heavy utilization changes. Mitigation: stronger utilization penalty and longer hold window for high-sensitivity customers (configurable per-customer)
Risk: Telemetry staleness during outages. Mitigation: mark stale windows and prefer fallback-safe defaults (regional affinity policy)
